summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and prior stents, was admitted for exertional chest pain, shortness of breath, orthopnea, and leg swelling. Initial evaluation ruled out acute myocardial infarction with normal EKGs and negative cardiac enzymes. He was found to have acute diastolic heart failure, treated with IV furosemide and transitioned to an increased oral dose of 60 mg daily. Cardiac catheterization revealed significant stent restenosis in the OM1, OM2, and circumflex arteries, which were successfully treated with cutting and kissing balloon angioplasty. His symptoms improved, and he was discharged home in stable condition on his prior medications with the addition of vitamin D for cardiovascular risk reduction. Follow-up was arranged with cardiology to discuss potential surgical options given the extent of disease.
